column1: L5 recomputes what actually happened from realised data, attributes P&L to the same economic effects Valuation used, and decomposes the gap between planned and realised value into four owned buckets.
L5 is the layer that makes the system improvable rather than merely operable: without it the engine can trade but nobody can say whether a change made it better.
L5's input is the ExecutionOutcome plus metered reality plus tariff sheets, and its output is the StateUpdate plus an internally recorded SettlementResult.
L5 is a total function with no I/O, no clock, no state and no randomness.
Settlement has no access to what the Planner intended: intentId crosses C4 as an opaque key and nothing else does.
Because ex-post accounting cannot be contaminated by ex-ante belief, Settlement's numbers are worth something as evidence against the Planner.
Settlement runs in two phases with a hard boundary, and the boundary is the point of the layer.

Phase A, Accounting, reads C4, the metered series, tariff configuration and the V artefact, produces realisedByEffect, peak state, qualification state and reconciliation results, and does not see the plan.
Phase B, Attribution, reads Phase A's sealed output plus the recorded C1, C2, C3 and PlanResult, produces the error buckets and the strategy-tag and mode conditioning, and does see the plan.
Phase A's output is content-hashed and sealed before Phase B starts, so no attribution question can reach back and change an accounting number.
Phase B is a comparison of two independently produced artefacts and is allowed to read the recorded plan precisely because it can no longer alter the ledger side of the comparison.
StrategyTag and shadowValue live on C3 rather than C4 and are read only in Phase B.
Keeping shadowValue on C3 is what makes the question of whether the quoting policy traded through indifference answerable without giving the accounting phase a view of intent.
Settlement trusts nothing upstream computed.
Settlement does not read a P&L number from Execution, does not accept the Planner's expected value, and does not carry a running total forward.

Every euro is recomputed from realised inputs: executed fills, awards and clearing prices, metered energy at the POI and the battery terminal, published imbalance prices, and the tariff sheets in force for that period.
Settlement recomputes using the same EconomicEffect enumeration Valuation used.
plannedByEffect and realisedByEffect are indexed by the same closed set of thirteen effects, so planned-versus-realised is a term-by-term comparison rather than an aggregate one.
A discrepancy localises to an effect and the ownership matrix maps that effect to exactly one view.
The exclusivity check that prevents double-counting in the objective prevents the same double-count in the ledger, because both sides use the same matrix.
A term counted twice in Valuation and once in Settlement shows up as a persistent, signed model error rather than as a plausible-looking profit.
If Settlement invented its own decomposition the two sides would drift and the four-bucket decomposition would be uncomputable.
Any new economic effect is added to the enumeration once and implemented on both sides in the same commit.
Meter data is provisional for days, imbalance prices for weeks, and network invoices reconcile over months.
A restatement is a new artefact carrying revisionOf and never an in-place edit.

The intraday provisional stage runs every tick on raw meter pulses and indicative imbalance, and can conclude the POI trajectory so far, whether a new peak candidate occurred, commitment status, and the energy-balance and SOC checks.
The intraday provisional stage cannot conclude anything price-final or anything about the month.

The D+1 provisional stage runs daily on a validated meter day and preliminary imbalance, and can conclude day P&L by effect to within imbalance uncertainty, whether the peak candidate is confirmed or rejected, and the slippage and forecast buckets for the day.
The D+1 provisional stage cannot conclude the final imbalance cost or the qualification status.

The M+X final stage runs on the settlement calendar with the final meter register, final imbalance and network invoice, and concludes the period's NetworkPeakCharge, the qualification outcome, the final P&L and isFinal true.
The M+X final stage is the reference and concludes nothing further.
X in M+X is a configuration value per DSO and per BRP rather than a constant.

The Planner never waits for final data: it consumes the latest state with peakIsProvisional and unsettledGapFrom set and treats the unsettled gap with its own modelled trajectory rather than assuming it was empty.
Provisional never overwrites final for the same settlement period, and isFinal is monotone per period.
Restatement is idempotent: re-running settlement on unchanged inputs produces a byte-identical artefact and no new revision.
A revision chain that grows without an input change is a defect.
Error buckets computed at D+1 are marked provisional and recomputed at final.
Attribution drawn from provisional buckets is directional evidence rather than a verdict, and the distinction is carried in the artefact rather than in a convention.
Phase A computes one signed EUR figure per EconomicEffect plus the mandatory unexplained bucket.
The settlement sign convention is that positive is revenue to the site, consistent with the battery frame, so charges and costs are negative.
Fees are always explicit and never netted into a price.
Volumes cross from kWh to MWh at the market adapter and nowhere else.
SpotEnergyValue is the sum over DA fills of the signed side times price times volume in MWh, less fees.
IdEnergyValue is the sum over continuous and auction intraday fills of the signed side times price times volume in MWh, less fees.
ReserveCapacityRevenue is the sum over blocks of awarded up and down times their clearing prices times block hours, less aFRR capacity fees.
Block hours come from the market calendar and are never a constant, because block length is a product attribute and changes.
ReserveEnergyRevenue is the sum over slots of activated up energy times its activation price minus activated down energy times its activation price, in MWh.
ImbalanceCost is taken from C4 as authoritative and cross-checked against imbalance volume times imbalance price, and a mismatch is a reconciliation finding rather than a silent substitution.
NetworkVolumetricCharge is the negative sum over slots of metered POI import in MWh times the volumetric rate.
LeviesAndTaxes is the negative sum over slots of metered POI import in MWh times the summed rates of the closed component list a delineation regime cannot reduce, mirroring TariffView's enumeration.
An unrecognised invoice line is a configuration error rather than an absorbed cost.
EnfgLevies is the negative of (21) in MWh times the summed reducible EnFG rates for the month.
Booking the reducible EnFG components on metered import rather than on (21) overstates the charge by the whole relief.
SubsidyRevenue is (32) in MWh times the sum over plants of ZFx times MAX[AWx − marktwertMonth; 0], the Marktprämie per § 19 EEG.
Under a common EEG vintage (32x) = ZFx·(32), so the per-plant premium sum collapses to one weighted premium.
CycleDegradation is the negative of the degradation cost per kWh times half the sum of charge and discharge energy.
StoredEnergyContinuation is V at the end-of-period measured SOC and state minus V at the start-of-period measured SOC and state.
Realised ActivationRisk is identically zero.
The (charge + discharge)/2 throughput convention must be byte-identical to the one OppCostView charges on the BatteryThroughput base.
If the degradation throughput conventions differ by a factor, every day shows a constant model error and nobody will know why for a month.
StoredEnergyContinuation is evaluated with the exact value-function artefact the Planner used, addressed by hash from the run manifest.
Using a refreshed V measures value-function drift and books it as P&L, which is wrong: drift belongs in the slow loop's own diagnostics rather than in the day's ledger.

ActivationRisk and the CVaR weighting on imbalance are decision-shaping penalties in the objective, and ex post there is no risk, only an outcome, which has already been booked to ReserveEnergyRevenue and ImbalanceCost.
The four-bucket decomposition uses the risk-free objective on both sides.
PlanResult reports the objective gross and net of risk terms so that the decomposition can use the risk-free figure.
Comparing a risk-loaded planned value against a risk-free realised value makes the engine appear to lose the risk premium every single day.
unexplained is total realised P&L less the sum over effects, is mandatory, and is never absorbed into a neighbouring effect.
A rising unexplained ratio is the earliest available signal that a term definition has drifted between L2 and L5.

The peak accounting engine runs per active tariff regime, regimes compose, and each produces its own accounting period, slot set and charge, tagged with its own effect so the exclusivity rules apply on the settlement side too.
Instantaneous POI import power is the metered import minus export divided by the slot hours, floored at zero because the charge is levied on import.
realisedPeakKw is the maximum of import power over the regime's period slots.
AnnualLeistungspreis takes all slots in the local calendar year and charges peakPrice times realisedPeakKw.
MonthlyLeistungspreis takes all slots in the local calendar month and charges peakPrice times realisedPeakKw per month.
AtypicalHlzf takes HLZF slots only, from the DSO's published window table for that year, and charges the HLZF peak price times the HLZF peak.
IntensiveUse takes all slots in the qualification year and applies a reduced rate conditional on qualification.
annualEnergyKwh is the sum of metered POI import over the year and annualPeakKw is the maximum import power over the year.
fullLoadHours is annualEnergyKwh divided by annualPeakKw, in hours.
flhMargin is fullLoadHours minus the configured FLH threshold of 7,000 hours, and energyMargin is annualEnergyKwh minus the configured energy threshold of 10 GWh.
qualificationMarginHours is the minimum of flhMargin and energyMargin divided by annualPeakKw.
Battery operation moves both the numerator and the denominator of full-load hours, so qualification is not a passive observation: every peak shaved and every kWh imported changes it.
Both qualification thresholds bind, so the published margin is the binding one, expressed in hours so the value function sees a single continuous distance to the cliff.
A boolean qualificationStatus tells the engine nothing until it is too late to act, whereas the margin lets V price the approach continuously and drives qualCritical.
Accounting period boundaries are local-calendar boundaries derived only via the CivilCalendar service against the manifest's pinned tzdata, with no UTC-offset arithmetic anywhere in the peak engine.
Any sum or maximum over a day iterates the calendar's slot set for that day and never a fixed count.
Both DST transition days are permanent fixtures in the peak-engine test set.
HLZF windows are local-time windows from a data table, resolved to SlotId sets through the CivilCalendar service.
An off-by-one-hour reset at a DST boundary either destroys a period's accumulated peak or carries it into the next one, and both are silent.
The delineation accounting engine evaluates the reference machinery exactly, from Z1 and Z2 and the tariff sheet alone.
The delineation accounting engine is the reference against which Valuation's linearisation is measured, and it is the only place in the system where the monthly formulas are evaluated.
In settlement Z1NB¼ is metered POI import, Z1NE¼ is metered POI export, Z2V¼ is battery charge energy and Z2E¼ is battery discharge energy.
In settlement (24)¼ comes from the settled day-ahead price series and the EEG vintage's § 51 or § 51b duration rule, and is a realised parameter rather than a belief.
Monthly aggregation in settlement runs (3) through (33) unchanged from the reference.
The route split identity (28) + (16) = (13) is asserted rather than assumed.
The loss-relief multiplier identity (16) + (19) = (16)·(5)/(6) is asserted rather than assumed.
The two delineation identities are cheap and catch a whole class of sign and attribution error.
Delineation period boundaries are Europe/Berlin civil-calendar month boundaries derived through CivilCalendar under the manifest's pinned tzdata, exactly as the peak engine's are.
The seven delineation accumulators reset at the month boundary, and a month containing a DST transition is a permanent fixture in the test set.
(12) is computed unconditionally even though the throughput invariant asserts the condition under which it must be zero.
Settlement never assumes what it can measure: the assumption belongs to the Planner, and a violated month must show as a booked cost and a fired invariant rather than as a silent divergence.
The A5 case adds only ZF, and under a common EEG vintage the AW forfeit is simultaneous so (24x)¼ = (24)¼, hence (32x) = ZFx·(32) and no per-plant accumulator exists.
Because every layer is a pure function of a recorded input, each error bucket is computable by re-running a layer with exactly one thing changed.
The computability of the buckets is the entire justification for the purity discipline.
b is the BeliefSnapshot used at the tick, recorded as C1.
b* is the outturn belief: the same series and schema with forecast values replaced by settled outturn, read from the bitemporal store at a later knowledge time.
Reading b* at a later knowledge time is a legitimate read rather than a lookahead violation.
Score(x; β) is L2's own term set at belief β evaluated risk-free on a trajectory or position vector, in EUR.
Scoring is possible because C2 is a set of declared terms, so the objective can be evaluated as well as maximised.
Book(x) is Phase A's accounting of x, the sum of realisedByEffect plus unexplained.
Ĵ₁ is Score(x̂₁; b), what the accuracy reference claimed on the belief.
Ĵ is Score(x̂; b), what the plan actually run claimed, and equals the sum of plannedByEffect.
A is Score(x̂; b*), the same plan scored on the outturn.
C is Score(x; b*), what was actually done scored on the outturn.
J is Book(x), what Settlement booked.

optimalityGap is Ĵ₁ − Ĵ, computed by re-solving the tick at Tier 1 on the identical C2 bundle with the same seed and SolveBudget shape and comparing objectives, and a large value means the fast path is costing real money on this class of day.
forecastError is Ĵ − A, computed by re-scoring the unchanged plan against b*, and a large value means the belief carried value the world did not deliver.
executionSlippage is A − C, computed by scoring plan versus realised positions under one common belief b*, and a large value means the trades could not be got or were got worse.

modelError is C − J, computed by valuing the realised trajectory with L2's terms and comparing against Phase A's independent accounting of the same trajectory, and a large value means Valuation and Settlement disagree about what a term means.
modelError carries a declared sub-bucket, linearizationGap, and residual modelError net of it is still asserted zero.
The four buckets telescope by construction to Ĵ₁ − J.
planned in the reconciliation invariant is the Tier-1 reference value Ĵ₁.
When Tier 1 was the tier actually used, Ĵ₁ = Ĵ, optimalityGap is zero, and the sum collapses to plannedByEffect total minus realised.
Both Ĵ₁ and Ĵ are recorded, and anchoring at Ĵ₁ is what gives optimalityGap somewhere to live, since a weak tier lowers both the planned and the realised side and is invisible in Ĵ − J.
executionSlippage splits into priceSlippage, unfilledOpportunity, feeDrag and deliveryDeviation.
priceSlippage is fills valued at intent price versus executed price, which is the narrowest reading of slippage.
unfilledOpportunity is the residual volume from C4 valued at b*.
deliveryDeviation is the controller's departure from setpoint within the corridor.
Without the unfilled term the slippage bucket cannot separate being wrong about value from being unable to get the trade, which is precisely why C4 §3 exists.
linearizationGap splits out of modelError as L2's λ-linearisation of the delineation machinery scored on the realised trajectory against §5.1's exact evaluation of the same trajectory.
linearizationGap is expected, budgeted and reported rather than a defect.
Without the linearizationGap split the zero-gap invariant fails permanently from the first day the delineation regime is active, and the most valuable test in the layer stops meaning anything.

linearizationGap is interpretable as exactly one thing, projection error, since V_del is evaluated arithmetically and never fitted, which is what makes a budget for it meaningful rather than arbitrary.
valueOfForesight is Score(Plan(Val(b*)); b*) − A, computed and reported alongside forecastError.
valueOfForesight answers what perfect information would have been worth and is the upper bound that separates a weak optimiser from an uncertain world.
valueOfForesight is not booked as a bucket because it does not telescope.

The telescoping identity is exact in algebra and inexact in practice, and the buckets are computed by independent re-runs rather than by differencing, specifically so that the residual is a test of the pipeline rather than a definition.
unexplainedError is (Ĵ₁ − J) minus the sum of the four buckets.
The reconciliation invariant warns when the magnitude of unexplainedError exceeds tolerance.

The legitimate sources of unexplainedError are bounded and enumerable: b* is itself an estimate while imbalance prices are provisional, a term-set version changed between plan and settlement, and tick-size rounding at C3.
Anything other than the enumerated sources of unexplainedError is a defect.
unexplainedError is a distinct quantity from the effect-level unexplained, the two are never netted and never reported as one number.
Phase B resolves each fillId to an intentId to a StrategyTag through the recorded C3 artefact and aggregates P&L per tag.
Per-tag P&L answers which strategy made money, which is the question that decides where the next month of engineering goes.
Directly attributable effects — SpotEnergyValue, IdEnergyValue, ReserveCapacityRevenue, ReserveEnergyRevenue and their fees — each descend from one fill and therefore one tag.
Joint effects — NetworkPeakCharge, CycleDegradation, StoredEnergyContinuation and ImbalanceCost — are properties of the whole trajectory and are not the sum of per-order contributions.
Joint effects are allocated by a declared rule: counterfactual removal of the tag's fills, re-run through the peak and SOC accounting, normalised across tags.
The joint-allocation normalisation residual is booked to an explicit unallocated line and never smeared proportionally.
Peak charge attributed naively makes PeakShave look free and Arbitrage look profitable, which is the exact misreading that leads to turning peak protection down.
An intent priced through shadowValue is legitimate only under the CommitmentCover tag.
Phase B reports the realised cost of cover as a separate line so that having to buy back at any price is visible as an operational failure rather than as a bad arbitrage day.
P&L and every error bucket are reported conditioned on DegradationMode, using ticksByMode and modeTransitions.

A DEFENSIVE week is supposed to earn less, and without conditioning a data-feed outage looks like a strategy regression and gets fixed by loosening risk parameters, which is the worst available response.
optimalityGap conditioned on tier is the number that decides whether the fast path ships, and it is reported as p50, p90, p99 and worst case, never as a mean, and conditioned on regime.
Escalations are reported so that having been on the fast path that day is always visible.
The conditioning output is a small cube of effect by tag by mode by tier.
The conditioning cube's purpose is to make a bad week answerable as attribution rather than as opinion.
Conditioning cells must be reported with tick counts, because a mode occupied for four ticks explains nothing regardless of its P&L.
The reconciliation checks run in Phase A before anything is sealed, are cheap, are the layer's own self-test, and several are the earliest available warning of a model defect.

The energy-balance check asserts that POI import minus export equals load minus curtailment-adjusted PV plus charge minus discharge within meter tolerance, and signals a sub-metering fault or an inverted sign convention.
The SOC consistency check asserts that measured SOC evolves per the efficiency-adjusted charge and discharge, and is the early-warning signal for efficiency and SOH model drift.
Persistent one-signed SOC divergence means η or the degradation model is wrong and it feeds modelError directly.
The fee reconciliation check asserts the sum of C4 fees equals fees booked per effect with no fee netted into a price, and signals a changed broker or venue fee schedule or a price that arrived net.
The levy base check asserts EnfgLevies is charged on (21) and never on (3), which is the single most expensive available mistake in the layer because it overstates the charge by the whole relief.

The SOC consistency check costs almost nothing to evaluate, needs no market data, and is the only check that catches a slowly wrong efficiency model before that model has quietly mispriced a quarter of arbitrage decisions.
Restatement is append-only: a revision is a new artefact with revisionOf set, the superseded artefact is retained, and the chain is acyclic, and violation is a HALT.
Zero-gap: settling the planned trajectory as if realised yields all four error buckets zero within tolerance, and violation fails the run.
Fees reconcile so that the sum of C4 fees equals the sum of fees booked by effect and no fee is netted into a price, and violation warns escalating to alert.
Every accounting period boundary and HLZF window is derived via CivilCalendar under the manifest's pinned tzdata with no UTC-offset arithmetic in the peak engine, and violation is a HALT.
While an IntensiveUse regime is active, qualificationMarginHours is published every tick and reflects both the FLH and the annual-energy threshold, and violation is a HALT.
isFinal is monotone per settlement period and a provisional artefact never supersedes a final one, and violation is a HALT.
Per-tag P&L plus unallocated sums to realisedByEffect per effect, and violation warns.
While monthly charge throughput exceeds η_d·E_usable/(1−η_rt), (12) = 0, and Settlement computes (12) regardless and publishes throughputBoundMet, with violation warning escalating to alert.
The delineation identities (28)+(16) = (13) and (16)+(19) = (16)·(5)/(6) hold within meter tolerance, and violation is a HALT.
The seven delineation accumulators are derived in Phase A from Z1 and Z2 and the settled price series alone, with no belief, forecast or planned quantity entering them, and violation is a HALT.
Settlement is the easiest layer in the system to test well, because it is pure, because conservation laws apply, and because the right answer is often computable by hand.
Same C4 and same manifest gives byte-identical C5 and SettlementResult.

Conservation is property-tested over generated outcomes rather than spot-checked: total booked P&L equals the sum over effects plus unexplained, energy in equals energy out within meter tolerance, and the sum of per-tag P&L equals the per-effect total.

The zero-gap test feeds Settlement the exact planned trajectory as realised — every intent filled at its limit price, metered series equal to the planned POI trajectory, imbalance zero — and asserts every bucket and unexplainedError is zero within tolerance.

The zero-gap test is the single most valuable test in the layer, because any non-zero bucket is a definitional disagreement between L2 and L5 that would otherwise masquerade as a real finding for months.
The synthetic day is a hand-constructed day with flat load, one price spike, one aFRR block and one peak event, where every effect and every bucket is computable analytically.
The synthetic day is the fixture that catches unit errors and is worth the afternoon it costs to build.

Restatement idempotency is tested by settling, restating with unchanged inputs and asserting no new revision, then restating with a corrected imbalance price and asserting exactly one new revision, the prior artefact intact, and the delta confined to ImbalanceCost and the buckets that legitimately depend on it.
Provisional-to-final convergence replays a period through intraday, D+1 and final and asserts the buckets converge monotonically in the magnitude of their own declared uncertainty.
Divergence across settlement stages means a provisional stage is concluding something it has no data to conclude.
Both DST transition days, a month boundary and a year boundary are permanent fixtures, and the peak reset is asserted to the exact slot.
The co-location identity test settles a month with load = 0, no clipping of discharge and (12) = 0, and asserts (21) = 0 to the cent.

The identity (16)+(19) = (9) = (3) holds independently of η, of the dispatch pattern, of AW and of prices, so any deviation localises a defect in the delineation chain with no modelling judgement involved.

The route split and relief multiplier are property-tested over generated months, and because both are algebraic identities of the published formulas a failure is always an implementation defect and never a data artefact.

The A5 collapse test asserts (32x) = ZFx·(32) exactly for two plants on a common EEG vintage with no per-plant accumulator required, then asserts the collapse is refused for a mixed case with one ungeförderte plant.
The month boundary test asserts the accumulators reset at the exact slot of the Europe/Berlin month boundary, with a DST-containing month as a permanent fixture.
A delineation month boundary off by one slot moves value between two months and is otherwise silent.

The qualification cliff test constructs a year landing just above and just below each threshold and asserts the margin is continuous through the crossing, that qualCritical fires at the configured distance, and that a single trade cannot cross the cliff without the flag having fired first.
Attribution invariance requires that permuting the order of fills within a slot leaves every bucket and every tag total unchanged.
Order sensitivity in attribution means an accumulator has hidden state, which would break purity.

Counterfactual soundness requires re-running each bucket's counterfactual twice on a recorded day and asserting byte-equality, and asserting optimalityGap is non-negative over a backtest in aggregate.
A single-day optimalityGap may be negative because a worse plan can get lucky, which is why a distribution rather than a point is required.
